item.aggregated_output:
Read /Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec13/luna/package.md. It holds image section 13 (Herkesi işiyle vadesine getiren gün) of the frozen surah commentary of surah 103: the Arabic text of the ayat concerned, the Turkish
commentary written on them, the words/roots/branch labels recorded in the frozen surah commentary, and the
whole surah in Arabic. The selected commentary defines your scope; the other inputs supply context.

Find, from the Hebrew Bible, the New Testament, and the Jewish and Christian literature around them (Targum,
Mishnah, Talmud, midrash, pseudepigrapha, Christian apocrypha, Church Fathers, Syriac homilies), every text an
advanced reader of this commentary should have beside it. Judge each text on what it says in its own place, not
on resemblance of a word. Weigh at least:

- paralel: the same figure, scene or story told in the other scripture;
- motif: a shared image, formula, liturgical act or ethical motif without a shared story;
- karsi_anlati: the Qur'an tells it differently, corrects or answers it; the difference is the point;
- soydas: a Hebrew, Aramaic or Syriac cognate of a key word of these ayat and how the other scripture uses it;
- yorum_gelenegi: Jewish or Christian interpretation of a parallel text that changes what the parallel means.

Before grading, work through every distinct scene, object, action, relation, formula and secondary sense
actually developed in the commentary, including any v16 augment additions. Recall direct formulations, repeated
occurrences, nonlexical parallels, relevant reversals and interpretive traditions. Do not let the title, first
scene or already quoted passages stand in for the whole page. For a Buluşmalar section, consider the particular
meetings between images its prose develops. Root/branch labels are not dictionary definitions, evidence of
cognacy or permission to import an undeveloped sense. Do this review internally; output only candidate rows.

Use the package's Semitic root table: for every Arabic root it lists, recall how the corresponding Hebrew or
Aramaic root is used across the Hebrew Bible, passages that play on the same consonants, and passages whose
wording shows a difference from what the ayah says. Propose such passages as soydas (shared root), motif,
paralel or karsi_anlati as fits, and name the basis in `basis` (the root, and whether it is the table's sound
correspondence or your own recollection). Same consonants with an unrelated sense are not a connection.

Every explanation must identify a particular detail or claim in the commentary, the corresponding detail in
the candidate's own context, and what the relationship adds. Shared vocabulary, a broad religious theme or
the same speaker alone is insufficient. Do not invent imagery that neither text supports. A shared word is
not required. Preserve indirect, secondary and contrary readings with a concrete connection; do not choose
one preferred reading. A parallel is not a dependence: say what the texts share, not who borrowed.

Check the speaker, addressee, action, negation and verse boundary in remembered context. Name a neighbouring
verse separately when its own contribution is necessary; proximity alone does not qualify it. Keep Hebrew,
Aramaic, Syriac and Greek quotations short and specific to the cited passage and witness. If exact wording or
numbering is uncertain, explain the connection and uncertainty in English instead of reconstructing a quote.
Label roots, dictionary forms and wording from the source commentary explicitly. Never combine verses into
one quotation. Distinguish WLC's written/ketiv stream from qere and other readings; name another witness when
you rely on it. Discovery is memory-only: the later verifier will open the actual texts and check your claims.

Include every candidate meeting this standard. There is no target list length. Strong means a direct,
specific correspondence, including a secondary feature developed in the prose. Medium means a specific
correspondence with an explicit interpretive bridge. Weak means a plausible, specific connection whose
uncertainty you identify; it still cannot be generic. Counter-narrative is a relationship kind, not weaker
confidence. Model agreement and a follow-up origin never make a claim verified.

Write one TSV row per distinct connection with exactly six tab-separated fields:

strength	tradition	kind	ref	basis	short_explanation

strength: strong, medium, weak. tradition: tevrat (Hebrew Bible and Jewish literature) or incil (New Testament and
Christian literature). kind: paralel, motif, karsi_anlati, soydas, yorum_gelenegi. ref: for the Hebrew Bible and
the New Testament an edition-qualified OSIS reference, one verse per row, no ranges
(WLC:Gen.22.2, WLC:Ps.1.3, SBLGNT:Matt.6.5; consecutive verses on their own rows).
Use Hebrew WLC numbering for Hebrew Bible candidates and SBLGNT numbering for New Testament candidates;
do not silently transfer English/KJV verse numbers. For other works give the work and its place as a reader
cites it (Targum Jonathan on Genesis 22:2;
Genesis Rabbah 56:1; Berakhot 60b; Ephrem, Hymns on Paradise 5:6; Protevangelium of James 8). basis: the words,
scene or motif that carries the link, in a few words. Strongest first. Keep distinct reasons or link kinds for
one passage in separate rows; exact repeated connections are unnecessary. Do not regrade an existing row.
The handoff groups references but preserves each distinct connection for an individual verdict.

Do not write a header row, rank numbers, Markdown, sections or prose outside TSV rows. Save the rows to
/Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec13/luna/list.tsv. End nonempty files with a newline. Zero qualifying candidates means an explicitly created
empty file. The saved file, not the chat response, is the deliverable.

## Frozen commentary (Turkish)

Hâkka, her insanı işiyle hak eden, vadesine getiren gündür: {ar:سميت حاقة لأنها تحق كل إنسان بعمله, tr:summiyet hâkkaten li-ennehâ tehukku kulle insânin bi-amelih, gloss:Hâkka diye adlandırıldı, çünkü her insanı işiyle hak eder, source:"ح ق ق,B006"}; {ar:الحاقة إشارة إلى القيامة لأنه يحق فيه الجزاء, tr:el-hâkka, gloss:Hâkka kıyamete işarettir, çünkü karşılık o gün gerekli olur, source:"ح ق ق,B006"}. Tek bir ifade surenin insanını, amelini ve hakkını birleştirir. O gün işler iyi ve kötü diye ayrılır {ar:الأعمال الصالحة والسيئة, tr:el-a'mâlu's-sâliha ve's-seyyie, gloss:iyi ve kötü işler, source:"ع م ل,B001"}, teraziler kurulur ve kimi eksik gelir {source:"خ س ر,B003"}, karşılık bağlayıcı olur {source:"ح ق ق,B002"}. İkinci ayetin ifadesi de cezayla açıklanır: {ar:لفي عقوبة بذنوبه, tr:le-fî ukûbetin bi-zunûbih, gloss:günahları yüzünden bir ceza içinde, source:"خ س ر,B004"}. Ters sabır burada ateşe götüren iştir: {ar:ما أعملهم بعمل أهل النار, tr:mâ a'malehum bi-ameli ehli'n-nâr, gloss:ateş ehlinin işini ne de çok yapıyorlar, source:"ص ب ر,B013"}.

Bu sahnede sure bir hesap kapanışı gibi okunur: zaman (birinci ayet) bir vadedir, kayıp (ikinci ayet) eksik çıkan bir hesaptır, istisna (üçüncü ayet) işi salih olan ve hakkı birbirine ileten kişilerdir. Düz anlatım "hak" kelimesinin aynı zamanda her insanı işiyle yüzleştiren günün adı olduğunu duyurmaz. Kur'an o günün adını üç kez tekrarlar: {ar:ٱلْحَآقَّةُ, tr:el-hâkka, gloss:gerçekleşen gün, source:69:1}, {ar:وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلْحَآقَّةُ, tr:ve mâ edrâke me'l-hâkka, gloss:Hâkka'nın ne olduğunu sana ne bildirdi, source:69:3}. Terazinin hafif gelmesi kayıp köküyle söylenir: {ar:وَمَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ, tr:ve men haffet mevâzînuhû fe-ulâike'llezîne hasirû enfusehum, gloss:tartıları hafif gelenler, kendilerini kaybedenlerdir, source:23:103}; aynı söz başka bir surede de gelir {source:7:9}; kısa bir surede kefeler ağır ve hafif diye ayrılır {ar:فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ, tr:fe-emmâ men sekulet mevâzînuh, gloss:tartıları ağır gelene gelince, source:101:6}, {ar:وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ, tr:ve emmâ men haffet mevâzînuh, gloss:tartıları hafif gelene gelince, source:101:8}. Terazi bir hardal tanesini bile kaçırmaz: {ar:وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ, tr:ve nada'u'l-mevâzîne'l-kıst, gloss:kıyamet günü için adalet terazileri kurarız, source:21:47}; zerre ölçüsü de görülür: {ar:فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًۭا يَرَهُۥ, tr:fe-men ya'mel miskâle zerratin hayran yerah, gloss:kim zerre ağırlığınca hayır işlerse onu görür, source:99:7}, {ar:وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍۢ شَرًّۭا يَرَهُۥ, tr:ve men ya'mel miskâle zerratin şerran yerah, gloss:kim zerre ağırlığınca kötülük işlerse onu görür, source:99:8}. Yapılan iş orada hazırdır: {ar:وَوَجَدُوا۟ مَا عَمِلُوا۟ حَاضِرًۭا, tr:ve vecedû mâ amilû hâdırâ, gloss:yaptıklarını karşılarında hazır buldular, source:18:49}; her insanın kaydı boynundadır: {ar:وَكُلَّ إِنسَٰنٍ أَلْزَمْنَٰهُ طَٰٓئِرَهُۥ فِى عُنُقِهِۦ, tr:ve kulle insânin elzemnâhu tâirahû fî unukıh, gloss:her insanın amelini boynuna bağladık, source:17:13}. İyi yaptığını sananların işleri ise tartıya bile girmez: {ar:ٱلَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا, tr:ellezîne dalle sa'yuhum, gloss:dünya hayatında çabaları boşa gidip de iyi iş yaptıklarını sananlar, source:18:104}, {ar:فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وَزْنًۭا, tr:fe-lâ nukîmu lehum yevme'l-kıyâmeti veznâ, gloss:kıyamet günü onlar için tartı kurmayız, source:18:105}. Sonunda iyi ile kötü ayrılır ve kötü üst üste yığılır: {ar:لِيَمِيزَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْخَبِيثَ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبِ وَيَجْعَلَ ٱلْخَبِيثَ بَعْضَهُۥ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ, tr:li-yemîzallâhu'l-habîse mine't-tayyib, gloss:Allah kötüyü iyiden ayırsın ve kötüyü birbiri üstüne koysun diye, source:8:37}, ve ayet {ar:أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰسِرُونَ, tr:ulâike humu'l-hâsirûn, gloss:işte kaybedenler onlardır, source:8:37} diye biter.

## Whole surah (Arabic)

/bin/bash -lc "cat > enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec13/luna/list.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Dan.5.27	Source root خ س ر; Aramaic חסר; table sound correspondence	The commentary labels khusr as loss and describes the person found deficient on the scales; Daniel's Aramaic חסר says Belshazzar was found deficient after weighing. The package table marks خ→ח, س→ס, ر→ר as an unverified regular correspondence, so this is a lexical echo in a matching context, not a proven etymology.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.5.27	scales; weighed and found deficient	The commentary's deficient account at judgment is closely matched by Daniel's weighing of Belshazzar and finding him lacking, which ends his kingdom. Daniel applies the measure to a ruler's historical sentence; the commentary extends the image to every person's recompense.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:1Sam.2.3	God weighs actions	Hannah's song says the Lord is a God of knowledge and actions are weighed by him; this gives a direct biblical image for the commentary's scales measuring each person's work.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.12.14	all deeds; good and evil	The commentary says every deed is present for judgment and good is distinguished from evil; Ecclesiastes says God brings every deed, including hidden things, to judgment, whether good or evil.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.17.10	each person repaid by deeds	The commentary makes the day bring each human being face to face with his work; Jeremiah's searching God repays each according to conduct and the fruit of deeds, making the individual accounting explicit.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.24.12	weigher of hearts; recompense	The commentary's scales miss no deed; Proverbs says the one who weighs hearts knows and repays each person according to work, joining scrutiny with recompense.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.18.30	each judged according to ways	The commentary describes a universal accounting by deeds; Ezekiel makes the verdict personal, with God judging the house of Israel each according to his ways and calling them to turn.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.12.2	resurrection; two outcomes	The commentary identifies the Hāqqa with resurrection and judgment; Daniel's sleepers awaken from the dust, some to everlasting life and others to disgrace, supplying an early Jewish scriptural scene of divided destinies.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Mal.3.18	distinguish righteous and wicked	The commentary's final sorting of good from evil is echoed by Malachi's promised renewed distinction between the righteous and wicked, specifically between serving God and not serving him.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Lev.19.17	rebuke one's neighbor	The commentary makes truth something people mutually urge on one another; Leviticus commands a person to rebuke a neighbor rather than bear sin with him, giving mutual moral correction a concrete communal form.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Job.14.5	Source root ح ق ق; Hebrew חֹק; table sound correspondence	The commentary labels Hāqqa with ح ق ق and explains the day as the due, appointed end of each person's account. Job says human days and months are fixed and their limit is set by God; חֹק is from the package table's unverified חקק correspondence, so the shared prescribed-limit sense is specific but etymology remains unproven.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.14.5	fixed human term	Job says a person's days are determined and God sets a limit that cannot be passed; this concretizes the commentary's reading of time as a term that brings each person to reckoning.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.31.6	just balance; integrity	Job asks to be weighed in a just balance so God may know his integrity; the commentary's scales test deeds, while Job turns the same image into a plea for an honest verdict on a life.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.11.1	honest weights; just scales	The commentary's judgment uses scales of justice; Proverbs condemns a deceptive balance and delights in a just weight, linking accurate weighing with moral justice in ordinary dealings.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.2.3	appointed time; wait	The commentary joins a fixed term with patience; Habakkuk says the vision awaits its appointed time and, even if delayed, is to be awaited. Its context is a promised vision, not a final judgment, but it makes waiting an active response to a fixed divine term.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zech.8.16	speak truth to one another	The commentary's mutual urging of truth has a close communal counterpart in Zechariah's command to speak truth to one another and judge with truth and peace in the gates; Zechariah locates this ethic in civic restoration.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Eccl.1.3	Source root ع م ل; Hebrew עמל; table sound correspondence	The commentary labels the deeds with ع م ل and presents work within a profit-and-loss account.
